## Per-Subject Overview

```{r}
#| label: subject-overview
#| results: asis
cat(as_raw_html(apa_gt(
  subj %>% select(dataset, group, n_channels, n_trials, n_discarded, n_kept,
                  pct_rejected, n_truncated, pct_flagged, pct_interpolated,
                  pct_outlier, median_baseline_sd, median_sme),
  "Data Quality by Subject (worst rejection rate first)")))
```

```{r}
#| label: subject-overview-plot
#| fig-height: 5
# Ordered by rejection rate rather than alphabetically: the reason to look at
# this plot at all is to find the tail, and an alphabetical axis hides it.
#
# A subject with no rejection rate at all is left out of the bars and counted
# in the subtitle instead. That is a deconvolved dataset: it is fitted against
# the continuous recording rather than averaged over trials, so it has no
# trials to reject and nothing to draw here. Leaving it in made fct_reorder
# fail outright (a level whose summary is NA gets no position), and drawing it
# as a zero-length bar would have been worse than the error: it would have read
# as the cleanest subject in the study.
rated <- subj %>% filter(!is.na(pct_rejected))
unrated <- nrow(subj) - nrow(rated)
if (nrow(rated) == 0) {
  cat(paste0("\n\nNo subject here has a trial rejection rate: every dataset in this report ",
             "was fitted rather than averaged, so there are no trials to reject. The ",
             "provenance table below reports what each fit excluded instead.\n\n"))
} else {
  note <- "Dashed line: median across subjects"
  if (unrated > 0) {
    note <- paste0(note, "; ", unrated,
                   " fitted (deconvolved) subject(s) not shown: no trials to reject")
  }
  sp <- rated %>%
    mutate(dataset = fct_reorder(dataset, pct_rejected)) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = pct_rejected, y = dataset)) +
    geom_col(fill = alz_blue, width = 0.7) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = median(rated$pct_rejected, na.rm = TRUE),
               linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
    labs(x = "Trials rejected (%)", y = NULL, subtitle = note) +
    alz_theme()
  print(sp)
}
```
